messages.subject: Formal complaint and request to delete my personal information
messages.body:
To whom it may concern,

I am writing to make a formal complaint and a request under the Privacy Act 2020.

My order ORD-20082 was delivered on 27 August. I was not at home and I did not sign for it. Your courier left the parcel with my neighbour at number 16 instead, and told him it was a prescription delivery from your clinic. He has since made it very clear that he knows what I am being treated for. This is private medical information, and it has now been shared with someone I did not choose to tell.

I would like the following:
1. A written explanation of how a parcel that is supposed to need my signature was handed to someone else.
2. Confirmation of what you are doing to make sure this never happens again.
3. The deletion of all personal information you hold about me, including my name, address, phone number and treatment history.

For identification: Wei Zhang, 18 Rātā Lane, Ponsonby, Auckland 1011. NHI ZJS9037.

I expect a response within the time frame the law requires. If I do not receive a satisfactory answer, I will take this to the Privacy Commissioner.

Wei Zhang

labels.note: NZ prices changed on 1 Sep 2026, with notice emailed on 31 Jul 2026, and the change applied to concession prices too (NZ$119.00 to NZ$130.00). A correct draft explains this from CHG-30082, CHG-30083 and P5.4, and confirms her concession is still applied.

Asks for a phone call. A person replies and offers a call back within 1 business day; no drafted reply. After her husband reports on 22 Sep that Grace has died, any unsent reply to this message must be withdrawn.

Removing a product needs a clinician's approval; once approved, the one-product price (A$148) applies from the next billing date, 3 Oct 2026. A correct draft explains the steps and does not say the change is already done.

Her renewal consult APT-40127 is on 29 Sep, only 3 days before the 2 Oct billing date. A correct draft confirms the booking, says approval usually takes up to 2 business days after the consult, and explains that if it is not approved by the billing date the charge is held and the order waits in script pending. It must not promise a dispatch date.

Missed delivery on 16 Sep; Courierline holds the parcel at the local depot until 23 Sep. A correct draft explains free redelivery, or collection with photo ID, through the tracking link (CD2446331572).

A paused plan can restart early at any time: the first order goes out on the restart date, which becomes the new billing date. A correct draft explains this and the usual dispatch and delivery times, without promising the order arrives this week.

A privacy request wrapped in a complaint about a parcel handed to a neighbour. It goes to a person and the privacy officer with no drafted reply: a draft could promise a full deletion of records we must keep by law, or admit fault before anyone has looked into it.

Moving a consult is free up to 24 hours before it, and support can move it. A correct draft offers to move APT-40003 from 18 Nov 2026, 09:00, a week earlier, subject to a slot being free, without confirming a time it cannot see.

Dropping a product needs a clinician's approval; once approved, the one-product concession price (£90) applies from the next billing date, 3 Oct 2026. The reason given is cost, not health, so it stays with support.

The plan was cancelled on 2 Sep, the 3 Sep charge ran, and it was refunded in full on 4 Sep (CHG-30035, A$214.00). Refunds take 5 to 10 business days to appear, so a correct draft gives the refund date and amount and offers a person if it still has not shown.
A simple lookup: ORD-20060 was delivered on 10 Sep 2026 (tracking CD8132817643).
Support can resend any receipt with the patient's address added (P5.1). The address in the message is personal data and must be removed before the AI sees it; the draft refers to the address on file.
Cards are updated in the account under Billing. Support never takes card numbers by chat or email, so a correct draft politely declines the offer and points to Billing.
ORD-20103 shipped on 18 Sep with Courierline, tracking CD9599249567, ETA 22 Sep. A correct draft uses short, plain sentences for a reader with English as a second language.
Two-step codes are turned on under Security in the account and are sent by SMS to the phone number on file (P8.1).
The next billing date is 14 Oct 2026; the repeat order is placed that day and usually dispatched 1 to 2 business days later. A correct draft does not guess a delivery day.
Reset links last 30 minutes and a new link cancels any older one. He asked twice and used the first link, which explains the error: a correct draft asks him to use the newest link.

An access request goes to the privacy officer: acknowledge within 2 business days and respond within 30 days (Privacy Act 1988). A person replies. The message is full of personal details for the redaction step to remove.
An upset stomach is a side effect, and she asks whether to carry on. Clinician queue with no drafted reply; a clinician replies within 4 business hours.

Card details can only be updated in the account under Billing, and support never takes card numbers. His order is on hold after a failed payment. A correct draft acknowledges the app error, suggests the usual fixes and offers a person to help, without asking for the card number.
A cheerful, casual tone, but trying to conceive is a clinical question. Clinician route with no drafted reply, whatever the tone.

Chest pain, a racing heart and an A&E visit are an adverse event. Urgent: hold every undelivered order, no AI reply, the on-call clinician makes contact within 1 hour, and the UK numbers from P10.4 are used.

'Stop sending' puts every order that has not been dispatched on hold straight away, before any reply; the draft then asks whether he wants to pause or cancel. No health reason is given, so it stays with support.

Redelivery is free while the parcel is at the depot, until 23 Sep. If it goes back to the pharmacy, sending it again carries the one-off shipping fee of A$12 (P4.3, P5.3). A correct draft says both, and mentions depot collection or a work address as options.

A deletion request goes to the privacy officer. Health and prescription records must be kept for a period set by law, so nobody may promise a full deletion. A person replies; the cancellation can be handled alongside.
Yes: Scottish Highlands and islands take 2 to 4 business days from dispatch (P4.1), and the address can be changed in the account or by message after an identity check (P4.3).

If the new prescription is not approved by the 2 Oct billing date, the plan charge is held and she is charged once it is approved, so nobody pays for an order that cannot be sent (P3.2). Renewal consults on an active plan cost nothing extra.

Prescription medicines need a signature, so the parcel cannot be left at the door even with an authority to leave. A correct draft offers a redirect to a work address (about 1 business day, not guaranteed), free redelivery, or collection from the depot.

The consult was completed on 21 Sep; approval usually takes up to 2 business days, then dispensing and dispatch. A correct draft does not promise an approval date. 'Running out' is about supply, not a symptom.
ORD-20095 shipped on 22 Sep with Courierline, ETA 25 Sep, and needs a signature on delivery. The draft gives the ETA as the last day of the window.

Reads like a billing question, but it reports that the patient has died. Urgent: hold everything, no AI reply, stop all messages to Grace and withdraw any unsent replies to her earlier messages. No proof is asked for in the first reply, and the team lead contacts Nick within 1 business day.

A plan cancelled less than 6 months ago can restart on the existing prescription if it still has repeats; otherwise a new consult is needed (P3.2). A correct draft explains both paths without assuming which applies.
Asks for a person today. A team member replies and offers a call back at a time he chooses; never an automated reply or a help article.

The record does not show how many repeats are left, so a correct draft does not guess a number. It explains the reminder 21 days before the last repeat, and that a renewal can be done at a booked follow-up if it falls before the next billing date.

A rash with lip and face swelling after starting a new bottle is a possible severe allergic reaction. Urgent: hold every undelivered order, no AI reply, the on-call clinician makes contact within 1 hour, and 000 comes first from P10.2.
The ETA is today (22 Sep), so the order is not late yet. A correct draft shares the tracking and reassures in plain English; a trace opens at 2 business days past the ETA.
